thread:
maya: quick flag — noticed canary for /v1/generate is getting 100% when a client sets X-Redwood-Canary: true even though weight is 10%. anyone else seeing header -> weight precedence?

oliver: hmm. can you paste the gateway rule that covers that path?

maya: here you go:
```yaml
- name: generate-route
  match:
    path: /v1/generate
    headers:
      X-Redwood-Canary: exact:true
  action:
    split:
      - service: model-canary
        weight: 100
      - service: model-stable
        weight: 0
- name: generate-weighted-default
  match:
    path: /v1/generate
  action:
    split:
      - service: model-canary
        weight: 10
      - service: model-stable
        weight: 90
```

sachin: right now our router evaluates rules top->bottom and first-match wins. header route is intentionally above the default weighted route so header wins. that config is working as designed.

emma: that makes sense, but the console's rollout UI claims canary is at 10% (global) which is misleading when header-based overrides exist. ops saw 100% and thought the weight had ramped.

devex: UX bug then — we should show "effective routing" and call out any higher-priority selectors (headers, cookies, ip). otherwise people assume global % applies to all traffic.

oliver: two options: 1) change rule ordering (fragile), 2) make header route set explicit metadata instead of a full split so it can be combined with global weight. e.g. header -> tag request, then weighted split by tag.

maya: example of 2):
```yaml
- match: headers X-Redwood-Canary:true
  action: set_header RBW-canary-tag: "1"
- match: path /v1/generate
  action: split_by_header:
    header: RBW-canary-tag
    mapping:
      \"1\": {model-canary: 100}
      \"\": {model-canary: 10, model-stable: 90}
```

sachin: nice. that preserves global weight while letting targeted clients opt-in. downside: more complex routing and requires header propagation in telem.

infra-bot: applied config generate-header-tagging to staging (deploy 7a3f).

emma: can we also tag telemetry spans with which selector fired? i.e. route_selector: header|weight|ip so dashboards show breakdown by selector.

devex: agreed. proposal: add a small pareto panel to Rollouts page that shows effective qps by selector + time series for canary error rate split by selector. low effort but high signal.

oliver: also add a console warning when a higher-priority literal match exists above a weighted rule for the same path. simple static analyzer when saving rollout.

maya: will open a quick RFC with config examples + console mock and a staging test plan. thanks for the ideas. :thumbsup:

sachin: one more thought — document recommended patterns: header opt-in vs cookie stickiness vs session-bucket for long-lived sessions. helps avoid accidental 100% routing.

maya: yep. i'll include that. tagging infra-bot notif once staging verifies.

infra-bot: staging smoke passed for generate-header-tagging (65s).

devex: great, thanks — this should avoid future surprises and improve observability.
